title: TT-Lang · Ragged softmax
content:
# TT-Lang · Ragged softmax

For `x` of shape `[R, L]` with logits in `[-80, 80]` and `lengths[r]` in `[0, L]`, compute the softmax of each valid prefix `x[r, :lengths[r]]`; entries outside the prefix and all entries of empty rows are 0.

Submit one Python file that defines:

```python
import ttl

@ttl.operation(grid=(1, 1))
def ragged_softmax(x, valid, out):
    ...
```

## How the judge runs your code

The judge imports your file and calls the operation named **`ragged_softmax`** exactly as shown in the signature; it
never calls anything else. Inputs are already **FP32, tile-layout tensors in device DRAM** on device 0 and the
output tensor `out` is preallocated with zeros. Do not open or close the device, do not read stdin and do not
print the answer. Only the TT-Lang operation runs on hardware; host-side code in your file runs once at import.

Padding: `x` and `valid` are padded exactly as in the ragged sum problem. `out` has the padded shape `(R_pad, W_pad)`; the judge checks the top-left `R × L` block, so padded positions may hold any finite value. Subtract the row maximum before exponentiating. Wide rows need more than one pass over the row. Guard the empty-row denominator with `ttl.max(denominator, eps)` rather than by comparing it with 1: the FPU rounds the row maximum, so a non-empty row's denominator can be slightly below 1.

Correctness: every logical output element must satisfy `|got - want| <= 0.0001 + 0.015625 x scale`, where
scale is |reference value| per element. The FPU rounds FP32 operands to about 11 significant bits, so the tolerance is deliberately
wider than FP32 epsilon; `ttl.exp` and other SFPU functions keep FP32 precision.

## Test cases

| # | R | L | padded (R_pad × W_pad) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 256 | 65 | 256 × 96 |
| 2 | 8,192 | 96 | 8,192 × 96 |
| 3 | 1,024 | 542 | 1,024 × 544 |
| 4 | 1,024 | 8,192 | 1,024 × 8,192 |
| 5 | 32 | 16,384 | 32 × 16,384 |
| 6 | 7 | 17 | 32 × 32 |
| 7 | 33 | 1 | 64 × 32 |
| 8 | 127 | 37 | 128 × 64 |
| 9 | 4,097 | 257 | 4,128 × 288 |
| 10 | 1 | 8,193 | 32 × 8,224 |

Inputs are generated from a fixed seed, so every submission sees the same data.

## Limits and quota

- One case at a time, **180 s wall time per case** including TT-Lang compilation, and 8 GB host memory.
- **Each account may submit at most 200 times to this problem** (pretests included); the quota is per account
  and per problem. The problem page shows how many your account has used. Test locally first; you cannot buy back
  a wasted submission.
- Runtime: tt-lang `1.1.10.dev20260921` (bundled ttnn, Blackhole p300c). `ttl.grid_size(dims=1)` and
  `ttl.node(dims=1)` are supported in this version. The starter file is attached as `starter.py`.

## Profile summary

Every accepted case returns a profile summary on the record page. The number that counts is the
**device time**: with the device profiler enabled (first invocation checked for correctness, then 3 warmups and
7 samples), the time from the first kernel start to the last kernel end over all cores, median over the samples. It excludes host dispatch, JIT
compilation and data transfers. The submission's score for the **leaderboard** is the geometric mean of the
device times of the 10 testcases; the leaderboard lists each account's fastest accepted submission
and its speedup over the single-core reference (1100.3 µs). Report device times in your report.

The record page also shows the cores your kernel used, its **effective bandwidth** (the bytes the problem must
read and write divided by device time; Blackhole DRAM peaks at about 512 GB/s), per-RISC kernel cycles per core
and, for diagnosis only, host-side timing of the call.

**Hardware counters.** A third pass reads the Tensix performance counters (FPU, SFPU, unpackers, packer, and the
three instruction threads) and reports, per testcase, how much of the kernel window each unit was busy, how often
each thread stalled and why (waiting on semaphores, SrcA/SrcB, unpack/pack/math idle). Use them in your report to
explain where time goes; the raw 85 counters are downloadable as CSV.
